description:
You are acting as a monitoring specialist and need to set up a simple SQLite database to track service alerts. In your home directory (/home/user), create a new SQLite database named alerts.db. Inside this database, create a table called "alerts" with the following columns: 
- id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT)
- service (TEXT)
- level (TEXT)
- message (TEXT)
- timestamp (TEXT)

Insert a single sample alert entry with the following information:
- service: "webserver"
- level: "critical"
- message: "Web service unreachable"
- timestamp: "2024-06-13T08:00:00Z"

Next, export the contents of the "alerts" table into a CSV file named /home/user/alerts_export.csv. The CSV file must include a header row with the column names ("id,service,level,message,timestamp") and one row with your completed entry. The CSV should be standard, comma-separated format (not semicolon or tab separated).

Finally, ensure that the new CSV file (/home/user/alerts_export.csv) exists and contains exactly one alert entry as described.
truth:
Before starting, there is no /home/user/alerts.db or /home/user/alerts_export.csv file. 
After completing the task:
- /home/user/alerts.db exists and contains a single table "alerts" with the given schema.
- The "alerts" table contains a single row with:
  - id = 1
  - service = "webserver"
  - level = "critical"
  - message = "Web service unreachable"
  - timestamp = "2024-06-13T08:00:00Z"

The CSV export file /home/user/alerts_export.csv must exist and contain the following content (using Unix line endings \n):

id,service,level,message,timestamp
1,webserver,critical,Web service unreachable,2024-06-13T08:00:00Z

No extra rows, columns, or formatting deviations are acceptable.
